title: Signal-Driven Opportunity Ledger for Emerging Model Features
creator: Priya Menon
description: Purpose: Build a repeatable ledger (catalog + probe matrix) that converts continuous market signals about emerging model features into prioritized product experiments and procurement triggers. Scope: taxonomy of signals (capability, latency, pricing, docs, release cadence), templated probe experiments (benchmarks, RAG probes, API compatibility), prioritization rubric, and a lightweight provisioning trigger map (when PM ops tags procurement/eng intervention). Deliverables: 1) canonical signal taxonomy doc in Confluence; 2) probe runbook (scripts, synthetic workloads) in Drive; 3) prioritization matrix integrated with the Model Watchtower dashboard; 4) sample procurement trigger playbook for Reserved GPU vs Hosted fallbacks. Success criteria: taxonomy adopted by at least two PM squads and the research team; 3 probe runs executed and triaged; priority signals surfaced automatically to Model Watchtower for next-cycle planning. Out-of-scope: vendor contract negotiations and legal procurement. Links: Confluence overview: https://confluence.redwood/company/model-signals/ledger (draft), Drive probe templates: https://drive.redwood/research/pm/signal-probes, Watchtower dashboard (prototype): https://dash.redwood/model-watchtower/probes. Acceptance criteria: taxonomy reviewed by Research and Eng-Platform, prioritization rubric documented and testable, 80% of identified high-priority signals have at least one matching probe in the runbook.
activity_log: 2026-02-21: Kickoff with Research & Eng-Platform. Agreed taxonomy seed (capability, latency, pricing, stability, docs). Action: Priya to draft taxonomy by 2026-02-26.
2026-02-26: Draft taxonomy posted to Confluence. Feedback from Eng-Platform: add kernel/quantization compatibility as a separate signal. Added.
2026-03-02: Probe templates (RAG latency probe, embedding throughput, API contract fuzz test) uploaded to Drive. Research requested sample datasets for finserv and SMB workloads.
2026-03-06: Engineering review: recommended adding KV-cache warmup patterns and continuous-batching variations to probe suite. Liam opened ENG-73122 to allocate infra for batch probes.

2026-03-10: Ran first synthetic probe for small-context summarization on two open models; observed 18% latency delta when prefix caching enabled. Logged results to Drive and flagged as medium-priority signal.
2026-03-12: PM sync: prioritized signals (1: quant-kernel incompatibility, 2: caching delta, 3: pricing shock potential). Drafted procurement trigger thresholds; seek legal input before automation.
2026-03-13: Internal demo to Product leadership. Approved to integrate top-3 signals into Watchtower prototype; assigned cycle work to Research for 2026-W11.
notes: Decision: use a light-weight numeric score (0-100) combining customer exposure, replacement cost, and likelihood to degrade. Rationale: balances economic and product risk.
Trade-off: deep contract probes (license/legal) require legal review and slow iteration. We'll surface contract-level flags as manual tickets rather than automated triggers for v1.
Review feedback: Design requested templated result visualizations to make Watchtower cards scannable by sales and solutions-engineering.
Follow-up: ask Solutions Engineering for two customer workload traces by 2026-03-20 to run domain-sensitive probes.
